gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EBL itself says its 1.5 V rechargeable lithium AA cells (the 3000 mWh budget pick) "Can't use for apple mouse and keyboard, Can't use for blink series". Blink's own spec sheet for the Outdoor 4 calls for "2 AA 1.5V lithium metal batteries (non-rechargeable)".
standout_why: Pages I opened: Charge-Test (cited). It already gives the CLR 4300 chargers (MX4, L4 Pro, VX4, L4, L8) and says not to assume any AA charger works, so the XTAR charger list is not new. Light And Matter (cited) says NiMH chargers won't work and warns against flashes, but says nothing about Blink or Apple input devices. RedRecs says only that XTAR "requires specific charger" and mentions no device exclusions. The Digital Camera World guide and its EBL review came back truncated, so I couldn't check them. I did not open reviewed.com, rottenwifi or elektroda. None of the pages I could read state EBL's own Blink and Apple exclusions, or that XTAR's older LC8 charger can't charge some 1.5 V cells.
decides: This narrows the budget pick rather than overturning the ranking. EBL rules its own 3000 mWh cells out of Blink cameras and Apple mice and keyboards, and Blink specifies non-rechargeable lithium-metal AAs. A shopper buying for a Blink camera or Apple peripherals should not take ChatGPT's 'best budget' EBL card. One of EBL's own bundle pages contradicts this by listing 'Blink cameras', which is a reason to flag the exclusion instead of trusting the listing. For the XTAR picks, charging needs a 1.5 V Li-ion charger that supplies 4.75–5.5 V. That rules out NiMH-only chargers, and XTAR's own LC8 has a stated exclusion. The Dealectric page should pair XTAR cells with the L4 Pro or L8 Pro, which charge both 1.5 V Li-ion and NiMH.
